Job Interviews & Mock Interview Skills

The Three Mandatory Questions, Mehrabian Non-Verbal Rule & STAR Method

Academic Lead:Mrs. Ishara Raviharee Weerasinghe(Senior Lecturer in English | Lecturer In Charge)
SLIIT City Uni • Professional Skills Assessment Standard
Curriculum Overview & Context

Demystifies the interview room as a two-way evidence-gathering dialogue. Breaks down Mehrabian's 93% non-verbal communication rule, the 6 C's (+ Confident) evaluation framework, and the STAR behavioral answering methodology.

Core Competencies & Learning Objectives

  • →Master the three foundational questions underlying every interview question.
  • →Evaluate candidate performance using the 6 C's (+ Confident) framework.
  • →Internalize Mehrabian's 7-38-55 Communication Rule for high-stakes interviews.
  • →Structure behavioral responses using the STAR methodology (Situation, Task, Action, Result).
  • →Employ precise grammatical tenses: Present for capabilities, Past for achievements, Future for vision.

The Three Mandatory Candidate Questions

The Core Subtext of All Interview Inquiries

An interview is not an interrogation; it is a high-stakes, two-way evidence-gathering professional dialogue. Regardless of how an interviewer phrases their questions, they are fundamentally probing three foundational truths.

1. Why are you here?:Evaluates genuine motivation, institutional alignment, passion for the company's specific product ecosystem, and career narrative continuity.
2. What can you do for us?:Assesses concrete technical competency, return on investment (ROI), domain proficiency, and ability to eliminate technical roadblocks.
3. What kind of person are you?:Uncovers cultural fit, emotional resilience under stress, ethical courage, and collaborative demeanor within multidisciplinary teams.

Mehrabian's Communication Rule (1971)

The 93% Non-Verbal Dominance in Human Appraisal

In 1971, Dr. Albert Mehrabian established that during face-to-face communication involving feelings and attitudes, literal words convey only a fraction of the total impression.

If a candidate's verbal statements are incongruent with their posture or vocal inflection, the hiring panel will unconsciously believe the non-verbal signals every single time.

Communication LayerPercentage ImpactInterview Manifestation & Best Practice
Body Language55%Upright open posture, authentic eye contact, firm handshake, purposeful gestures, professional attire.
Tone of Voice38%Warm resonance, moderate cadence, pitch modulation, eliminating uptalk and hesitant vocal fry.
Spoken Words7%Concise technical vocabulary, precise terminology, absence of colloquial slang and filler sounds ('um', 'like').

The STAR Behavioral Answering Methodology

Engineering Quantifiable, High-Impact Evidence

Top-tier tech corporations (Google, Amazon, Microsoft) utilize behavioral interviewing based on the psychological premise that past performance is the best predictor of future behavior.

The STAR formula guarantees that the candidate delivers structured, evidence-backed answers without meandering into superficial generalizations.

S - Situation:Establish the specific organizational context, project background, or corporate crisis (15% of answer time).
T - Task:Clarify the precise technical objective, deadline pressure, or explicit challenge you were assigned to solve (15% of answer time).
A - Action:Articulate the exact technical and interpersonal initiatives YOU led. Focus on 'I' rather than a vague 'we' (50% of answer time).
R - Result:Deliver quantifiable business or technical outcomes, metrics achieved, and lessons learned (20% of answer time).
Grammatical Tense Precision
“Use Present Tense for current capabilities ('I am proficient in TypeScript'); Past Simple / Present Perfect for completed achievements ('I engineered the database schema'); Future Tense for organizational vision ('I will optimize your query latency').”
— Interview Communication Protocol

Connecting Theory to Practice: Undergraduate & Developer

Reflective analysis connecting Job Interviews & Mock Interview Skills to coursework at SLIIT City Uni, software engineering projects (LA'CEDRA, TechMart, ApPoint), digital systems at LA'CEDRA, and collaborative teamwork.

01. Meaning & Conceptual Core

A professional job interview is a high-stakes, structured two-way evidence-gathering dialogue where hiring evaluators assess organizational cultural alignment, emotional composure, and concrete problem-solving capability. Success depends on mastering structured answering methodologies (STAR) and synchronizing verbal lexical precision with authoritative non-verbal communication.

02. Key Theoretical Concepts Acquired
→The Three Mandatory Candidate Inquiries: 'Why are you here?' (passion), 'What can you do for us?' (hard competency & ROI), 'What kind of person are you?' (culture fit & emotional stability).
→The 6 C's (+ Confident) Evaluation Framework: Clear, Concise, Concrete, Correct, Coherent, Courteous, and Confident.
→Mehrabian's Communication Rule (1971): 55% Body Language (posture, eye contact), 38% Tone of Voice (pitch, inflection), 7% Spoken Words.
→STAR Behavioral Answering Methodology: Situation (context), Task (objective/blocker), Action (specific technical/interpersonal execution), Result (quantifiable impact & lessons).
→Grammatical Precision: Present Tense for ongoing habits, Past Simple for completed accomplishments, Future forms for strategic career goals.
IT//EQ
03. Industry Imperative — Why This Matters in Tech

Technical candidates frequently fail interviews not because they lack coding proficiency, but because they ramble incoherently, fail to articulate their problem-solving thought processes, or project nervous defensiveness. In agile engineering teams, communicating why an architectural trade-off was made under pressure is just as critical as writing the code.

Core Academic Takeaways

01.

93% of an interview impression is non-verbal (55% body language + 38% vocal tone); words comprise only 7%.

02.

Every question is a disguised variant of: Why are you here? What can you do for us? What kind of person are you?

03.

The STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result) ensures candidate answers are concise, evidence-driven, and quantifiable.

04.

Successful candidates research company specifics and exhibit the 6 C's (+ Confident); unsuccessful candidates exhibit generic answers and fidgeting.

Reflective Learning Prompt & Target Action

“Review your latest mock interview recording: where did your vocal tone or body language contradict your spoken words?”

Target Action:Record three 2-minute STAR responses on camera, reviewing for vocal inflection, eye contact, and elimination of filler words.

Assessment Viva Voce Protocol (Random Question Box)

4 Questions
Randomized Assessment Questions:
  • Q01.Deconstruct Mehrabian's 7-38-55 communication rule in the context of a virtual technical interview.
  • Q02.Deliver a 90-second STAR response describing how you resolved a critical git merge conflict.
  • Q03.List the 6 C's (+ Confident) of interview evaluation and explain how they prevent rambling.
  • Q04.What grammatical tenses should you strictly apply when discussing current skills vs. past achievements?
Defense Protocol & Conduct:
  • Maintain upright, grounded posture with arms resting uncrossed on table or lap.
  • Maintain 3-5 seconds of sustained, respectful eye contact with the interviewer before blinking naturally.
  • Speak with deliberate vocal pace (130-150 words per minute), pausing deliberately between STAR sections.
